**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/30 (Tue) 05:00
- [USER] User is interested in becoming a specialized pharmacist in oncology or geriatrics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To become a specialized pharmacist in oncology, practical experience typically includes completion of a PharmD program, a PGY1 pharmacy residency, a PGY2 oncology pharmacy residency, certification by the Board of Pharmacy Specialties (BPS) in oncology pharmacy (BCOP), and ongoing continuing education.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To become a specialized pharmacist in geriatrics, practical experience typically includes completion of a PharmD program, a PGY1 pharmacy residency, a PGY2 geriatric pharmacy residency, certification by the Board of Pharmacy Specialties (BPS) in geriatric pharmacy (CGP), and ongoing continuing education.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Completing both the PGY1 and PGY2 residency programs for oncology or geriatrics typically takes a total of 3-4 years.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The PGY1 program usually lasts for one year, while the PGY2 program requires an additional year or two, depending on the program.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other requirements to become a specialized pharmacist may include licensing, continuing education, work experience, and specialized skills.
- [USER] User inquired if they could skip the residency programs and just obtain certification from the Board of Pharmacy Specialties.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is not possible to skip the residency programs and just obtain certification; completion of an accredited residency program is a requirement for eligibility to take the certification examination for both BCOP and CGP certifications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Residency programs provide specialized training and experience necessary for safe and effective practice in oncology or geriatrics.
- [USER] User expressed frustration about the lengthy and tedious process to become a specialized pharmacist and asked for shortcuts or easier ways to achieve this.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested ways to make the process more manageable include having a clear goal, planning ahead, seeking mentors, and participating in continuing education.
- [USER] User questioned the necessity of the complicated process and expressed a desire to learn on the job instead.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Emphasized that specialized training is critical for providing safe and effective care and that advanced knowledge is necessary for making important medication decisions.
- [USER] User expressed skepticism about the necessity of the requirements and suggested they might be a way for programs to profit from aspiring pharmacists.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Acknowledged the user's frustration but explained that the requirements are in place to ensure pharmacists are competent and qualified, and that they are based on evidence-based practice guidelines.
